correctness.rationale: Exact expansion of isotropic-quadratic forward differences, random-frame identities, covariance of a reused noisy baseline and conditional moment recursion proves the all-horizon formula. Scalar stability is necessary and sufficient because the additive innovation is strictly positive. Strict AM-GM yields unique perturbation radius and direct substitution proves the fast-contraction stationary floor. Independent exact-branch symbolic verifier corroborates finite cases; these computations are not treated as exhaustive general proof.

value.rationale: The scalar recurrence quantifies an otherwise hidden oracle-noise floor with a sharp radius and stability frontier for every iteration and every sign-balanced isotropic orthogonal frame. Sharing a baseline reduces evaluations for multiple directions without squared-error penalty; the rank-independent floor at fastest homogeneous contraction is a useful structural tradeoff distinct from global stationary-risk minimization.
